Q1. Which statement best describes a reasonable physics approximation?
A. It is always acceptable to treat a human arm as a point particle when studying
how the elbow joint rotates.
This confuses rotational motion (where size/shape matters) with translation of the center of
mass.
B. When tracking a hiker’s location on a map over several kilometers, modeling
the hiker as a point mass is usually adequate.
Over kilometer-scale motion the object’s size is negligible compared with the displacement, so
a point-mass model is appropriate.
C. If you neglect air drag in a calculation, you are never allowed to describe the
situation as “in vacuum.”
This incorrectly treats “vacuum” as forbidden language rather than a modeling idealization
used to ignore air effects.
D. None of the above is correct.
Option B is a standard and valid approximation for large-scale position changes.
questions.stem: Which statement best describes a reasonable physics approximation?

options.text: It is always acceptable to treat a human arm as a point particle when studying how the elbow joint rotates. This confuses rotational motion (where size/shape matters) with translation of the center of mass.

If you neglect air drag in a calculation, you are never allowed to describe the situation as “in vacuum.” This incorrectly treats “vacuum” as forbidden language rather than a modeling idealization used to ignore air effects.
None of the above is correct. Option B is a standard and valid approximation for large-scale position changes.

Q2. Which of the following equations is correct?
A. 1 nickel = 1 $
This mistakes a 5-cent coin for a full dollar.
B. 1 nickel = 0.5 $
This incorrectly treats a nickel as fifty cents instead of five cents.
C. 1 nickel = 0.05 $
A dollar is 100 cents and a nickel is 5 cents, so 5 = 0.05 $.
D. 1 nickel = 5 $
This reverses the conversion and produces a value that is orders of magnitude too large.

Q7. A basketball is launched with speed v0 at an angle θ above the horizontal.
What is the ball’s speed at its maximum height (neglect air resistance)?
A. v0.
This ignores that the vertical component of velocity decreases to zero at the top.
B. v0 cos θ.
At maximum height the vertical velocity is zero, so the speed equals the unchanged horizontal
component v0 cos θ.
C. v0 sin θ.
This mistakenly takes the initial vertical component as the speed at the top, even though it
becomes zero there.
D. 0.
Only the vertical component becomes zero at the top; the horizontal component generally
remains nonzero.

Q11. A constant force F⃗ = (2.50 N) ˆı−(6.00 N) ˆȷ acts on a particle while it moves
along the x-axis from x = 1.20 m to x = 6.80 m. What work (J) is done by the
force?
A. −33.6 J
This incorrectly includes the y-component as if there were vertical displacement along the x-axis
motion.
B. 14.0 J
The displacement is ∆⃗r = (5.60 m)ˆı, so W = F⃗ · ∆⃗r = 2.50 × 5.60 = 14.0 J.
C. 33.6 J
This magnitude comes from multiplying |Fy| by ∆x, which is invalid because Fy is perpendicular
to the displacement.
D. 8.40 J
This results from using the wrong displacement (e.g., subtracting endpoints incorrectly or using
the wrong force component).
